verses.verse:
ऋषभषड्जयोमध्ये कोमलो ऋषभो भवेत्।
स्वरस्थानानि चैतानि द्वादशानि प्रकल्पयेत्।।२२।।
verses.text: Between Ṛṣabha and Ṣaḍja is komal Ṛṣabha. Thus one should devise these twelve svarasthānas (note positions).

commentary.text: That is, between Ṛṣabha and madhya Sa is the place of komal Ṛṣabha. In this way place all twelve notes in the form of marks.

An example is given here on the basis of the rule above. Suppose we printed the roundness of a pipe or bamboo on paper and found its roundness to be about 6 sūt [a small unit of length]. Then I measured the inner girth of that roundness, opened it out and measured it: the paper that sat inside in the shape of a round ring of 6 sūt became, after opening out, about 17 sūt long, that is 1 inch 7 sūt. Now we named this paper (antaḥparidhimāna, measure of the inner circumference), and gave it a short name too, miti (the measure). Then we cut a pipe 7 times as long as this miti and found it came to about 12 inches. When a mukharandhra (mouth-hole) was made at one end, the pipe from the mouth-hole to the end was some ten and a half inches long. Now, first of all, in order to place tāra Ṣaḍja, a mark was made at a distance of four inches two sūt down from the mouth-hole and taken as tāra Ṡa. And the far end of the pipe was taken as madhya Sa, since it is between these two Sas that we have to place the 12 notes. If the space between the two Sas were divided into 6 equal parts and Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni placed in order, the bānsurī would certainly be out of tune. For as we go on making holes moving upward, its area keeps decreasing, and in the same proportion the distance between the notes (svarāntara, interval) also keeps decreasing. It is with this fine point in mind that the rule above had to be made the basis. So in the figure the marks will not be at equal distances from bottom to top.

But after the marks are made, the holes on those marks must be made in order. By the rule above, madhya Ṣaḍja should not be taken to be the cut end of the pipe that stands naturally open. So, measuring with the miti (the measure of the inner circumference), a hole should be made at a distance of six miti from the mouth-hole, its girth about half the girth of the pipe; and about one miti below that hole should be the far end of the pipe. If a bānsurī 7 times the miti is to be made, make the madhya Sa hole at the distance of 7 times. And if a bānsurī longer than 7 times is to be made, place madhya Sa at that same distance too. But do not place the remaining notes by the rule above; for that we shall give some additional rules later. The rule above is only for those bānsurīs that are 6 or 7 times their miti long. See the figure ahead.

Here, the place where the author has taken Ṣaḍja to be is, in the view of players, the place of the Pañcama note. Still, for the convenience of beginning sādhakas (learners), the Ṣaḍja given above is accepted. If, out of habit, the first hole on the bānsurī, which is the lowest, is taken to be Pañcama rather than Ṣaḍja, then for them another method of placing the notes is set out. Although there is no special difference between this method and the one above, it is written to remove some people's doubts.
